dl031_calibration.automation_approach: A regex-based scanner (new script: scripts/scan_dl031.js) can identify definition-match candidates by: (1) filtering items with CognitiveLevel in {Remember, Understand} AND DifficultyScore >= 3; (2) computing the stem-to-correct-choice word overlap ratio (word-level Jaccard similarity); (3) checking for definition-stem patterns ('Which of the following', 'refers to', 'is defined as', 'is a', 'represents the'). High-confidence matches (overlap > 60% + definition pattern) can be auto-downgraded. Borderline cases (40-60% overlap) are routed to a verification queue for human/agent review. After verification, a bulk-apply script downgrades Difficulty from 'Moderate'/'Difficult' to 'Easy' and DifficultyScore to 1. Post-change verification (governance guard, validator, hash recapture) is fully script-chained.
dl031_calibration.false_positive_risk: MODERATE — 20-30% of flagged items may be legitimate Moderate items with definition-like stems but sophisticated distractor engineering. The verification queue handles this. Risk is contained: false positives result in slightly over-downgraded difficulty labels, never in content errors.

dl035_remediation.automation_approach: The core authoring task (writing 117 choice-specific distractor explanations) is inherently judgment-based and cannot be meaningfully automated. AI-assisted drafting can produce template suggestions, but final text requires ACMA Part 1 domain knowledge appropriate to each distractor. Automation value is limited to pre/post verification scaffolding: a script can (1) inventory every empty non-CC EW slot by QID, (2) verify post-remediation that all 117 slots are non-empty and >= 50 chars, (3) flag any slot that still triggers Rule 6. The verification automation saves ~1 hour across 117 fields. A template-extraction tool could pre-fill distractor skeletons based on the item's Topic/MicroTopic fields, reducing draft time from 3 min to ~2 min per field, but this is AI-assisted drafting, not true automation.

clone_replacement.automation_approach: Metadata scaffolding can be fully automated: a script can pre-fill all structural fields (QuestionID, Part, Section, SectionName, SectionTags, ItemType, ItemStyle) from the QID convention and section template, leaving only content fields (Stem, Choices, ExplanationCorrect, ExplanationWrong*) for authoring. Post-authoring verification can be script-chained: read the authored item from the pack file, verify CorrectChoice matches the independently derived answer, run governance guard Rule 2/6/9, and log discrepancies. The S899 model of 20 items/session can potentially increase to 25-30 items/session with automated metadata scaffolding and verification chaining — a 25-50% throughput improvement. However, the core creative work (stem design, distractor engineering, explanation authoring) remains irreducible manual/agent labor. The 15 min/item ceiling can be reduced to ~11 min/item (3 min metadata + 8 min authoring + 0 min verification).

certification_workflow.automation_approach: A certification pipeline orchestrator (scripts/pipeline_orchestrator.js — already exists but manual-invoke) can script-chain all 7 structural scans + verification steps into a single command. The orchestrator would: (1) accept a QID list or section range; (2) sequentially invoke identity_validator → readiness_scorer → candidate_engine → dl008_scanner → dl026_scanner → governance_guard_tests → validator_suite; (3) aggregate output into a per-batch certification report; (4) auto-generate the REVISION_HISTORY.md entry template with QID list and pass/fail counts. The only remaining manual step is the CAQS 6-dimension verification (requires accounting judgment). Baselines recapture (hashing, table update) can be added to the orchestrator as a post-certification hook. A full certification pass drops from ~20 min/batch to ~8 min/batch.

qc_workflow.automation_approach: A post-change verification script (scripts/post_change_qc.js) can execute the entire QC pipeline: (1) run governance guard test suite; (2) run validator suite; (3) verify QID counts; (4) recapture SHA-256 hashes for all 13 runtime-critical files; (5) diff against stored baselines from CURRENT_BASELINES.md; (6) flag any unexpected hash drift; (7) auto-update CURRENT_BASELINES.md if hashes changed and a 'baselines-update' flag is set; (8) generate a QC report. The entire workflow drops from 15 min to ~3 min of human decision time (interpreting unexpected flags).
